# OpenCodeProjectSettings

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.OpenCode` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/OpenCode/OpenCodeProjectSettings.cs#L16)

What the OpenCode window knows about this project: the instructions every chat starts from,
and the prompts a new chat suggests.
These belong to the project rather than to one developer - everyone on the team should get
the same agent - so they live under ProjectSettings and are committed with it, unlike the
per-user choices in [`OpenCodePrefs`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-opencode/OpenCodePrefs). Edited on the Assistant page of the
VR Framework project settings.


## Fields

### DefaultInstructions {#defaultinstructions}

Starting point for a project that has not written its own. Short on purpose: it is sent
with every message, so every line costs context for the whole conversation.

```csharp
public const string DefaultInstructions = "You are working inside the Unity project \"{project}\" (Unity {unity}), which is built on the VR Framework (VRF) package. The Unity Editor is open while you work.\n\n- The scene open in the editor is {scene}. The current selection is {selection}.\n- Never touch Library/, Temp/, Logs/ or obj/ - Unity owns them.\n- When you create, move or delete an asset, keep its .meta file with it.\n- Scenes and prefabs are YAML with cross-referenced file IDs. Prefer the Unity MCP tools to change them when those are available rather than editing the YAML.\n- The user reads your replies in a narrow editor panel: keep them short."
```
